plan.title: release:run (#6845 S5): publish, draft flip and promote by reconciliation, and the runbook

narratives.Description: After the tag, the operator still watches the npm publish, flips the draft release and decides on promotion by hand, and a run that stops part-way leaves the state to work out by hand (#6878, S5 of #6845). This story builds the publish-watch, draft-flip and promote phases of `deft release:run` by reconciliation with GitHub and npm, the GitHub-release check on a resumed finish, and the operator runbook. It builds clauses 6, 9, 10, 11, 24, 26, 27, 28, 29 and 30 of the accepted #6845 lean 7032154033 (split comment 7048165729).
narratives.Overview:
After the tag, the operator still watches the npm publish, flips the draft release and decides on promotion by hand, and a run that stops part-way leaves the state to work out by hand. This story adds the publish, draft-flip and promote phases of `deft release:run` (#6845) by reconciliation with GitHub and npm, and replaces the Stable cut runbook. In the clauses, B is the cut base (the fetched delivery-branch tip), T is the tree of the release commit and M is the merged release commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Approved scope. The approval covers source tree T at M, built by the tag-triggered npm workflow at M, and release notes read from M. The draft release notes and the upgrade banner are read from M with `git show`, not from the local checkout. The run publishes only by the tag push and never dispatches the manual republish workflow; a failed publish run stops the run.
- [ ] Resume by reconciliation. The run record (`.deft-scratch/release-run/<version>.json`) keeps B, T, the PR number, the grant ids and the retry counts. Each phase decides from observed state. A tag that peels to M only locally is pushed; a remote tag that peels to M is done; a tag on any other commit stops the run. npm is done only when both packages carry the version on `maintainer` and the tag-triggered workflow run, with its post-publish fixture, concluded `success`; a run in progress is waited on; a failed run stops. The GitHub release is done when it exists for the tag, and the flip is done when it is not a draft. An expired or spent grant that an unfinished phase needs stops the run and names the mint command. Any other state stops the run; nothing is overwritten.
- [ ] Promote. The promote phase runs only with its up-front grant and after the post-publish fixture passed. It first looks for a promote-latest workflow run for the version: a run in progress is waited on; a run that concluded `success`, with both packages on `latest` at the version, is done; a failed run or a partial state stops the run without a new dispatch. With no run found it dispatches once. An unknown dispatch result after the grant was spent stops the run; it is not retried.
- [ ] Docs. The release skill Stable cut runbook and `docs/RELEASING.md` become this command, its approval step and the post-run pin steps. The merge-freeze rule and the routine-cut skip path leave the runbook.
- [ ] Given one package published and a failed publish workflow run, then the run stops and does not dispatch a republish.
- [ ] Given an expired `release-publish` grant when the draft flip is due, then the run stops and names the mint command.
- [ ] Given a promote grant minted up front and a green post-publish fixture, then promote dispatches once.
- [ ] Given both packages on `latest` and the promote workflow run still in progress, when `--resume` runs, then it waits and does not mark promote done; given a failed promote run, then it stops and does not dispatch again.
- [ ] Given a spent promote grant and an unknown dispatch result, then the run stops.
- [ ] Given no promote grant, then the run ends with `latest` unchanged.

Refs #6845

Depends on: S4 (#6877).

narratives.UserStory: As a release operator, I want `deft release:run` to watch the tag-triggered npm publish, flip the draft release and promote `latest` (only with its up-front grant) by reading GitHub and npm on every run and `--resume`, so that after the up-front mint I no longer watch, flip or promote by hand and a stopped run never redoes a done step.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. packages/core/src/release/run-reconcile.ts (new): the reconciliation phases.
   - Publish watch: read the commit the remote v<version> tag peels to (M) and the tag-triggered npm-publish.yml run (event push, branch v<version>) whose head is M. No run yet is waited on for the Phase 7 npm wait budget; a run in progress is waited on; a run that did not conclude success stops, and so does a post-publish two-pass fixture job that did not conclude success (#6966: a deferred Pass 2 still reads success). Then both packages must carry the version on the maintainer dist-tag (registry wait). The run never dispatches the manual republish workflow (clauses 1, 2, 5).
   - Draft flip: read the GitHub release for the tag. Published is done; missing or unreadable stops; a draft needs the run's release-publish grant. A recorded grant that is expired, spent or revoked is replaced only by a newer active grant for the same <version>@<T> target; otherwise the run stops and names the mint command. Then the run-bound draft flip (#6875) (clauses 2, 6).
   - Promote: only with the recorded release-promote-latest grant (none: SKIP, latest unchanged). Look for a promote-latest run (workflow_dispatch npm-publish.yml run created since the publish run, with the promote job not skipped): in progress is waited on; success with both packages on latest at the version is done; failure or a partial state stops without a dispatch. With no run found and a usable grant it dispatches once (grant spent before dispatch); a failed or unknown dispatch result stops and is not retried; a spent grant with no run found stops and names the mint command (clauses 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 10).
2. packages/core/src/release/run.ts: publish-watch, flip and promote call run-reconcile.ts; header and help text name the reconciliation.
3. packages/core/src/release/finish.ts: under the run binding, a GitHub release that already exists for the tag (draft or published) is done; Steps 12 and 13 do not create it again (clause 2).
4. Docs: the release skill Stable cut runbook (content/packs/skills/skills-pack-0.1.json, rendered to content/skills/ and content/.agents/skills/) and docs/RELEASING.md become `deft release:run`, its approval step and the post-run pin steps (pnpm update -w @deftai/directive-runtime@<v>, then pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, then the pin PR). The merge-freeze rule and the routine-cut skip path leave the runbook; the release skill's Routine vs hard cut section follows the Step 5 CI reuse rule (#6791 carry-over). docs/RULE-MAP.md regenerated if the rule counts move (clause 4).
5. Colocated vitest suites (run-reconcile.test.ts, run.test.ts, finish-run-tag.test.ts) and a content-contract test release_run_runbook.test.ts; changelog fragment changelog.d/6878-release-run-reconcile.md.

issueCommentThread.body:
Carry-over from S1 (#6791, PR #6898). Step 5 now reuses green CI automatically on an identical tree, and `docs/RELEASING.md` § Step 5 CI reuse describes this. Two places still contradict it, and S5's runbook rewrite should fix both:
- `content/skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md` § Routine vs hard cut (around lines 247-259) still says green tip CI is "a precondition, not a replacement for Step 5". That file was outside S1's scope.
- Greptile flagged remaining routine-cut wording in `docs/RELEASING.md` near line 103 on the final #6898 head ("Release instructions disagree"). Re-check the whole routine-cut section against the Step 5 reuse rule.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Carry-over from the #6869 arc (scoped to `--repo` inference only). The pin-bump lockfile problem from the 0.130.2 cut belongs to the release run's post-run pin steps:
- Swapping the `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` row made pnpm refuse the old lockfile entry (`ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION`). `pnpm update -w @deftai/directive-runtime@<version>` rewrote it.

Requested test for S5 (and S3 should print the same step):
- [ ] The pin preparation regenerates the lockfile for the new pin.
- [ ] `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes on the pin branch before the pin PR opens.
